newsitem.title: JAPAN: Prosecutors questioning DKB vice president -- Jiji.
newsitem.headline: Prosecutors questioning DKB vice president -- Jiji.

text.p: Prosecutors are questioning the current executive vice-president of Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB), Jiji news agency reported on Tuesday.
Jiji reported that Ichiro Fujita, a current executive vice-president, is being questioned by prosecutors.

The report came soon after the scandal-tainted Japanese bank unveiled a fresh line-up for its top management, supplanting an earlier reshuffling announced late last month in which Fujita was due to become the new president.
Jiji also said that several other DKB executives, including a former executive vice-president and former executive and managing directors, are also being questioned.
A DKB spokeswoman said she could not immediately confirm the report, although she said the bank plans to hold a news conference later on Tuesday.

Present and former DKB officials have been arrested on suspicion of giving 11.78 billion yen in uncollateralised loans, via a DKB affiliate, to Kojin Building Co, a realtor run by racketeer Ryuichi Koike's younger brother.
The loans, which were extended between July 1994 and September 1996, are suspected of violating Japan's Commercial Code.
